$comment: Pinned disclosed upstream state for SEC-2 and SEC-7.
This file is NOT an exclude list and NOT a threshold reduction. Each gate below
still runs in full; the rubric asserts that the finding set it produces is
EXACTLY this set. A new finding, a changed finding, or a disappeared finding all
FAIL the gate and force a human back to this file. Emptying an entry is the only
way a finding leaves the rubric, and that requires the upstream fix to have
landed.
Rationale for pinning rather than letting the gate stand red: a permanently-red
gate reports the same colour whether or not a NEW vulnerability appeared, so it
detects nothing. An exact-set assertion keeps detection alive while representing
the known, unfixed, upstream-owned state honestly and visibly in every report.
The audit covers the whole installed graph, not `--prod`. Dev dependencies are
not outside the boundary: they execute in CI with the checkout and the runner's
environment in reach, and they resolve from the same lockfile as the shipped
build. A dev-only advisory is disclosed here as its own entry with its own owner
and sunset, never excluded by scope. The full-graph audit currently reports NO
advisory at ANY severity — not merely none at or above the gated one — which is
why the list below is empty. See the devalue record further down for the last
advisory that was in the graph and what closed it.
GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p (ws, high) was disclosed here and is RETIRED at the
greater-v0.13.0 pin bump. The entry's own sunset named this exact condition:
"Delete this entry at the first `greater` CLI pin bump whose adapters release
resolves ws >= 8.21.0." greater-v0.13.0 bumped graphql-ws to 6.2.0, which
resolves ws@8.21.0, so the vulnerable range >=8.0.0 <8.21.0 no longer contains
the installed version. `pnpm audit` reports zero advisories across the WHOLE
graph, not only --prod.
The entry is deleted rather than kept with a note, because SEC-2 asserts the
finding set is EXACTLY this list: a retired advisory left in place fails the
gate just as loudly as a new one appearing, and that symmetry is the whole
design. An empty list is not a weakened gate — a new advisory now fails SEC-2
immediately, which is the strongest this check has been.
DEPENDABOT ALERT #1 — devalue, GHSA-9rgm-9g3h-6x36 / CVE-2026-81176, 'Svelte
devalue: DoS via malformed input', medium (CVSS 5.3,
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L, CWE-770), published 2026-09-17,
reported against manifest pnpm-lock.yaml. Recorded as narrative here and NOT as
an entry in `advisories` below, for two reasons that are each load-bearing.
First, THE FIX LANDED: this was closed by a bump, not disclosed as unfixed, and
`advisories` is the exact set of advisories the audit STILL reports — an entry
for a resolved advisory fails SEC-2 as 'disclosed but not reported', which is
the retirement path working rather than a gap in it. Second, SEC-2 gates high
and critical and this is medium, so it was never in the asserted set at any
severity. It is written down anyway because the decision needs a reason and the
reason is not recoverable from a lockfile diff: a reader who finds only
'5.8.2 -> 5.9.4' cannot tell whether the alert was fixed, dodged, or never
examined.
alert number:       Dependabot #1 on equaltoai/contentus, open against the
default branch when this bump was made
advisory:           GHSA-9rgm-9g3h-6x36 / CVE-2026-81176. `devalue.parse`
prior to 5.9.2 fails to reject out-of-bounds indices, so a
crafted payload makes devalue alternate between array
representations and do work quadratic in payload size.
Availability impact only: C:N/I:N/A:L.
affected range:     < 5.9.1, first patched version 5.9.2
previously locked:  devalue 5.8.2 — INSIDE the affected range
path:               . > svelte@5.56.8 > devalue (transitive; devalue is not
named in package.json)
now locked:         devalue 5.9.4
decision:           BUMP, not accept
WHY BUMP RATHER THAN ACCEPT, given the reachability finding below. svelte
declares `devalue: ^5.8.1`, so 5.9.4 is inside svelte's OWN declared range and
the fix costs one lockfile re-resolution: `pnpm update devalue --lockfile-only`
replaced four lines, all of them devalue, with no package.json edit. No
`pnpm.overrides` entry was added, and that absence is the point — an override
would force every consumer of devalue to a version chosen here, when the range
svelte actually declares already admits the patched release. Reach for an
override only when a parent's range caps below the fix; this one does not. A
fix this cheap is not worth an open alert, and 'unreachable' is a property of
svelte's internals, which this repo neither owns nor pins: a future svelte
patch could put `parse` on a path contentus ships, and the lockfile would then
carry a known-vulnerable function under a green SEC-2.
REACHABILITY, examined rather than assumed, because 'transitive' is not a
verdict and neither is 'medium'. The advisory's own precondition is that the
application calls `devalue.parse` with untrusted data. Contentus does not:
devalue is imported nowhere under src/ or scripts/, FaceTheory does not import
it, and svelte's only two call sites are `devalue.uneval` — the SERIALIZE
direction, not `parse` — both inside svelte's server internals
(internal/server/hydratable.js, internal/server/renderer.js). `devalue.parse`
appears nowhere in svelte's source. In contentus's own build output devalue is
present in build/server/handler.mjs and absent from build/client, so the only
path it sits on is a server-side serialization of values contentus's own render
pass produced. The precondition is unmet at this head. That is what makes this a
hygiene bump rather than the repair of a live defect, and it is recorded so the
next reader does not have to redo the walk to learn whether the alert mattered.
POST-BUMP STATE: `pnpm audit` over the whole installed graph — not `--prod`, and
at every severity rather than only the gated ones — reports 'No known
vulnerabilities found'. The pinned set below is empty and the audit agrees with
it at every severity, which is a stronger agreement than SEC-2's
high-and-critical gate asks for. Alert #1 closes on the default branch when this
bump merges; it was fixed on a branch and filed against another, which is why
the alert still reads 'open' on GitHub while this file records it as resolved.
If a future lockfile re-resolution puts devalue back below 5.9.2 the advisory
returns at moderate severity and SEC-2 will NOT catch it — the gate's floor is
high. This record is the only thing in the repo that would notice.

must_pass_reason: These are the two integrity properties the gate exists for: every vendored
component file the manifest records is present, and nothing extra is sitting
under the vendored root. They are non-negotiable and are asserted PASS.
SEC-7 fails if either regresses, regardless of anything disclosed below.

disclosed_failures.name: NPM Dependencies
summary: The blog face's registry manifest requires the shared `content` module,
which carries MarkdownRenderer.svelte and CodeBlock.svelte and pulls a full
Markdown rendering chain. The face's own Article.Content deliberately
refuses to render Markdown — lesser owns canonical rendering — so the
renderer arrives through a sibling module the reading surface never uses.
Contentus declines to install that chain: installing it to satisfy a
checker would ship a second canonical renderer and break the renderer-
authority invariant this repo exists to hold. See
docs/consumption/renderer-authority.md.
sunset: Delete this entry the day the blog face stops requiring the `content`
shared module, or the day the Markdown chain moves out of it. The same day
$comment: VERSION RANGES MOVED AT THE greater-v0.13.0 PIN BUMP, and the finding did not.
The same thirteen dependencies are still required by the blog face's registry
manifest and still declined here; three of them are simply required at newer
ranges by the v0.13.0 registry (@apollo/client ^4.0.9 -> 4.2.9,
@apollo/client-react-streaming ^0.14.0 -> ^0.14.5, viem ^2.47.14 -> ^2.55.10).
SEC-7 asserts the disclosed set EXACTLY, so a moved range reads as one finding
retired and another appearing — which is the gate working. The strings are
updated to what `greater doctor` now reports; nothing was installed and the
reason for declining is unchanged.
graphql@^16.12.0 LEFT THIS LIST AT M2, and it left by being installed rather than
re-declined. Contentus now validates the GraphQL documents it sends against
lesser's pinned canonical schema (scripts/audit-graphql-documents.mjs), and that
validation uses graphql-js — the reference parser and validator — as a
DEVDEPENDENCY at build time. It is not the Apollo runtime client and not part of
the declined Markdown chain: nothing under src/ imports it, and the small
same-origin transport in src/lib/cms/graphql.ts is untouched. The twelve entries
still listed above are still declined, for the reasons stated.
The version is greater's declared floor, not the newest release: the registry
asks for ^16.12.0, so the pin is 16.14.2. Installing 17.x instead would raise a
fresh `greater doctor` Manifest-vs-Required-Floors warning, and the honest answer
to a floor a peer declares is to meet it, not to disclose past it. A pin is not a
place to put problems.

summary: components.json declares the CLI's default alias set. Contentus vendors
only the faces and shared modules it consumes, so src/lib/components/ui and
src/lib/primitives are never created. Creating empty directories to silence
a checker would be exactly the cosmetic workaround this rubric refuses.
These are pinned so that a THIRD warning — which would mean a real alias
regression — fails SEC-7.
`Alias Path: utils` WAS pinned here and is now retired, which is what this
list is supposed to do. M4 vendored the social face's shared modules, whose
registry manifest places notificationGrouping.ts at `lib/utils/`; the `utils`
alias target src/lib/utils therefore exists and the check passes on its own.
It was removed rather than left in place because SEC-7 fails a disclosed
finding that has started passing — the retirement path working as designed,
not a silencing.
